AUTHOR: Wang
TITLE: Shrinking Encoding with Two-Level Codebook Learning for Fine-Grained Fish Recognition
VENUE: 2016 ICPR 2ND WORKSHOP ON COMPUTER VISION FOR ANALYSIS OF UNDERWATER IMAGERY (CVAUI 2016)
SPECIES: eulachon, pollock, rockfish, salmon, squid (Cam-trawl); 43 classes in Chute multispectral set
DATA: Cam-trawl dataset (NOAA, in-trawl stereo camera); Chute multi-spectral dataset
D_EV: Sec. III.A: 'In our evaluation, the standard 10-folds cross-validation is adopted.'
R_EV: Sec. III: Cam-trawl and Chute datasets each evaluated separately with 10-fold cross-validation; no cross-dataset testing.
C_EV: Sec. II: 'Finally, a linear SVM classifier is trained and used for fish recognition.' (no score threshold or reject option)
E_EV: Table II: 'Accuracy Compared with Different Methods' - only Acc (%) and mAP (%) reported.
ARCH: Dense SIFT + bag-of-features with two-level codebook shrinking encoding (ScSPM/LLC) + linear SVM
NOTE: Cam-trawl = in-trawl camera in the wild (included). Fish crops detected by GMM before classification. Chute multispectral dataset (43 classes incl. crabs, invertebrates) appears to be on-deck chute imagery, coded only as secondary. Descriptor weight >0.6 shown in Fig.5 is visualization, not classification threshold.
